Methodology and data scope

For Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe, OpenJev 4B, OpenJev 32B and Microsoft Decision-1, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, AUROC and average latency are reported for ToxiGen, HateCheck and AEGIS2, with equal weights of one third per dataset; Detect-Jailbreak and all other datasets are excluded from these means. These six models use prompt v1 at threshold 0.5, each with its own successful samples; OpenJev 4B, OpenJev 32B and Microsoft Decision-1 results are supplied internal summaries. Local model latency is elapsed/processed from each dataset's v1 / 0.5 run, averaged equally across datasets; OpenJev latency comes from the corresponding supplied summary entries. Missing quality results or complete timing for any required dataset make the corresponding mean N/A; the dataset scope is not reduced. Dynamo CPU, Dynamo GPU (A100), Dynamo GPU (L4), Mistral and Warden use user-supplied averages retained as provided. These means are not averaged again; their prompts, thresholds and timing protocols were not supplied. Unreported F1 or AUROC values are N/A; F1 is not inferred from average Precision/Recall. The latency axis uses a logarithmic scale above 1 ms. Successful samples and timing protocols are not aligned across models; this is a descriptive reference, not a fair ranking. All six metrics are visible together in a two-column grid (one column on narrow screens). Model order is fixed across panels, with light group separators; methodology can be expanded separately. Additional dataset-scope limitation: no internal dataset was available when the six models above were evaluated, so their averages use only the three shared datasets. Other model evaluations may also have included an additional internal dataset.
